subject: Request: VAT on August invoice and corrective credit
messages:
From: Elena Morris <billing@sunrisetech.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:13:00 -0400
Subject: Question about August invoice VAT charge

Hi Sean,

We received the August invoice (INV-2025-08-0023) this morning and our accounting team flagged an unexpected VAT line for €4,800. We are registered for VAT in Ireland and were expecting the reverse-charge treatment to be applied (zero VAT on Redwood's invoices). Can you confirm why VAT was charged and either send a corrected invoice or advise the process for a refund/credit?

I've attached the invoice we received (PDF).

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Billing Lead, Sunrise Tech
[Attachment: INV-2025-08-0023.pdf (PDF)]

Quick note: I'm looping in Marissa (Finance) and Michael (Billing Ops) so we can investigate and get you a corrected document quickly. Also let us know if you prefer a credit applied to next invoice or a direct refund.

We'll aim to get this resolved today.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 14:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question about August invoice VAT charge

Hi Elena — Marissa from Finance here. Thanks for the heads up and for confirming details over Slack earlier. We reviewed INV-2025-08-0023 and found that the tax code mapping for your EU reverse-charge flag didn't apply correctly when the invoice was generated — it resulted in VAT calculated on the gross amount.

What we've done so far:
- Recalculated the invoice with reverse-charge (VAT 0%) and produced a revised invoice (INV-2025-08-0023-revised.pdf).
- Prepared a credit memo for the VAT portion: €4,800 gross (CRM-credit-memo-5491.pdf).
- Noted that the credit can be issued as a refund (bank transfer) or applied as a credit to your next Redwood invoice.

Next steps for Sunrise Tech (confirm please):
1) Confirm the VAT ID you want on the revised invoice (please reply with the exact string).
2) Tell us whether you prefer the credit applied to next invoice or a refund to the original payment method.

Timing: If you confirm the VAT ID and preference by EOD today, we will publish the corrected invoice and either issue the credit memo (applied immediately) or start a refund, which can take 2-5 business days to post depending on your bank.

I've attached the revised invoice and the credit memo stub for your records.

Thanks — sorry for the inconvenience; we'll get this cleared up.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Finance Manager | Redwood Inference

Our VAT ID is IE1234567V. We'd prefer Redwood apply the credit to our next invoice rather than a refund — that keeps our reconciliation simpler.

Two quick questions:
- Do you need any specific documentation from us to support the reverse-charge claim?
- For audit purposes, will you include a note on the revised invoice stating the reverse-charge reason so our accounting can file it correctly?

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Elena

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morris <billing@sunrisetech.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 09:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question about August invoice VAT charge — Confirmation and next steps

Hi Elena — quick update and confirmation:

1) Marissa has posted the revised invoice (INV-2025-08-0023-revised.pdf) to the Drive link and created a CRM credit memo (CRM-credit-memo-5491.pdf).
2) Per your preference, we've applied the €4,800 credit to Sunrise Tech's account and it will automatically offset your next Redwood invoice. You will see the credit applied on your September invoice cycle.
3) For audit trail: the revised invoice includes a note in the VAT section — "Reverse charge applied per EU VAT Article 44; buyer VAT ID: IE1234567V". That should be sufficient for your reconciliation.
4) No further documentation required from Sunrise unless your local tax counsel requests additional paperwork — we'll keep the credit memo and internal audit notes on file for 7 years per our retention policy.

If you change your mind and want a direct refund instead, let me know and we'll initiate a bank transfer (refund timeline 2-5 business days after initiation).

Thanks again for flagging this — sorry for the hiccup. Please reply if anything looks off.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
